items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.one_liner: An actively exploited Oracle access control flaw has been added to the KEV catalog, requiring immediate patching for those managing WebLogic or HTTP server infrastructure.
items.summary: CISA has added a critical Oracle vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog following evidence of active exploitation. The flaw, CVE-2026-21962, affects Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-ins, potentially allowing unauthenticated attackers to bypass access controls. Federal agencies are required to prioritize remediation of this vulnerability under Binding Operational Directive 26-04. CISA strongly encourages all private sector organizations to patch this flaw immediately to prevent total asset compromise.
key_facts: CVE-2026-21962: Improper Access Control in Oracle HTTP/WebLogic
Affected Products: Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in
items.bottom_line: Organizations must prioritize patching CVE-2026-21962 to prevent unauthenticated attackers from gaining total control over Oracle-based web infrastructure.

items.title: Actively Exploited Oracle WebLogic Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Access Critical Data
items.one_liner: This is a critical, actively exploited RCE in a major enterprise middleware component that requires immediate patching or mitigation.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-21962 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following evidence of active exploitation against Oracle HTTP Server and WebLogic Server. This maximum-severity flaw (CVSS 10.0) allows unauthenticated attackers with network access via HTTP to gain unauthorized access to instances or modify critical data. While Oracle released patches in January 2026, threat actors have continued to target this and other persistent WebLogic RCE flaws. Federal agencies are mandated to apply the necessary fixes by August 27, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Organizations running Oracle WebLogic must patch immediately as this CVSS 10.0 flaw is being actively exploited in the wild.

claims.text: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to modify or access critical data.

claims.text: Threat actors are targeting this flaw alongside other known WebLogic RCE vulnerabilities.

items.title: India approves transfer of missile technology to defence industry
items.one_liner: India approves transferring DRDO conventional missile technology to private defense industries to build an indigenous missile force.
items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh approved the transfer of technology for all conventional missile systems developed by the DRDO to the Indian defence industry, enabling private sector and MSME manufacturing. Previously, production was restricted largely to Bharat Dynamics Limited, DRDO in-house facilities, and joint ventures like BrahMos Aerospace. Systems eligible for the transfer include the ASTRA BVRAAM, RUDRAM anti-radiation missiles, VSHORADS, NAG anti-tank guided missiles, and Naval Anti-Ship Missiles, while strategic assets like Agni and K-series missiles are excluded. The initiative aims to scale domestic defense manufacturing, reduce import dependence, and build a dedicated conventional missile force following lessons from recent conflicts in West Asia.

Excluded Systems: Agni and K-series missiles
items.bottom_line: Opening DRDO missile tech transfer to private Indian firms fundamentally shifts national defense production from PSUs to open industrial manufacturing.

Iranian officials asserted readiness to counter the pressure, while commodity analysts questioned the direct effectiveness of the new package given existing enforcement levels and ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Granite 4.2 LLMs: How They're Built
items.one_liner: IBM's Granite 4.2 reasoning LLMs feature extended context windows, native tool calling, and an explicit thinking mode switch.
items.summary: IBM released Granite 4.2, a family of dense, decoder-only reasoning LLMs available in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes under the Apache 2.0 license. Pre-trained from scratch on approximately 15 trillion tokens via a five-phase strategy, the models extend context windows up to 512K tokens and feature a multi-stage reinforcement learning pipeline. The 8B and 30B models include agentic RL to operate tools, execute code, and drive terminals in sandboxed environments. Every model includes a thinking / low-effort / non-thinking mode switch along with native OpenAI-compatible tool calling.
items.bottom_line: Granite 4.2 delivers open-weight reasoning models with native tool calling, configurable thinking budgets, and agentic RL training.

claims.text: Granite 4.2 is our first family of dense, decoder-only reasoning LLMs, released in three sizes: 3B, 8B, and 30B.

items.title: Agentic Security: A Systematization of Tools, Failure Modes, and Design Laws for LLM-Driven Penetration Testing
items.one_liner: This research provides a formal framework for understanding why your automated red-teaming agents might fail or exceed their intended scope.
items.summary: This research systematizes operational failures in agentic security systems that use LLMs to plan and execute penetration testing. Through an evaluation of ten common security tools, the authors identify recurring failure modes in unattended pipelines and introduce the Integration Friction Index to measure engineering and organizational costs. The study models these systems as stochastic policies within deterministic mediators, revealing that long-lived sessions often lose critical evidence over time. Crucially, the findings demonstrate that system prompts are insufficient for enforcing scope and budget, as they do not effectively constrain the actual execution of tools.
items.bottom_line: Scope and budget enforcement in agentic security cannot be delegated to system prompts because prompts do not reliably constrain what the system actually executes.

items.title: Beyond Over-Refusal: Defending Indirect Prompt Injection via Latent Instruction Manifolds
items.one_liner: AEGIS is a new adaptive ensemble guard designed to mitigate indirect prompt injection in LLM agents without incurring severe over-refusal.
items.summary: Indirect Prompt Injection attacks present major barriers to the safe deployment of LLMs integrated into complex ecosystems like code agents by exploiting the model's inability to distinguish instructions from data. Existing guardrails often fail by introducing high latency or severe over-refusal rates. To address this, researchers propose AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding), which extracts instruction-sensitive projectors and uses a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism across network depth. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that AEGIS achieves superior detection performance against heuristic and optimization-based attacks compared to baseline methods.
key_facts: Tool/Framework: AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding)
items.bottom_line: AEGIS separates instructions from data intrinsically via multi-layer consensus to defeat indirect prompt injections without over-refusal.

items.title: On Predicting Vulnerability Severity Using In-Context Learning: An Industrial Case Study
items.one_liner: Medium-sized open-source models like CodeLlama2-7B can locally predict vulnerability CVSS scores to provide privacy-preserving industrial triage.
items.summary: Modern software systems require scalable vulnerability severity assessment, but manual CVSS triage fails to scale with growing disclosures, while cloud LLM services present confidentiality concerns. Researchers conducted an industrial case study predicting CVSS v3.1 scores from vulnerable C/C++ code snippets using in-context learning with local, open-source LLMs. By comparing proprietary data against the Big-Vul dataset, the study evaluated models including CodeLlama2-7B, CodeLlama2-13B, Mistral-7B, gpt-oss, and GPT4o-mini. Results indicate that medium-sized models like CodeLlama2-7B can approximate cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by output-constraining prompts.
key_facts: Models evaluated: CodeLlama2-7B, CodeLlama2-13B, Mistral-7B, gpt-oss, GPT4o-mini
items.bottom_line: Locally deployed open-source code models can effectively approximate cloud performance for automated CVSS severity prediction without data leakage.

claims.text: Our results show that medium-sized open-source code models, particularly CodeLlama2-7B, can approximate the best cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by lightweight, output-constraining prompts, offering a practical, privacy-preserving building block for severity triage in industrial settings.

items.title: SkillBloat: Token Amplification Attacks via Skill Injection in LLM Coding Agents
items.one_liner: A new 'denial-of-wallet' attack vector that exploits the very 'skills' you use to extend your coding agents.
items.summary: SkillBloat is a new token amplification attack targeting LLM coding agents through malicious "skill" injection. This economic resource-abuse threat causes agents to consume significantly more tokens than necessary, potentially leading to massive unexpected costs. The attack uses a two-phase framework: first screening for effective amplification mechanisms and then using an LLM to iteratively rewrite the skill for maximum impact. Testing on real-world benchmarks showed that SkillBloat can achieve up to 10x token amplification, proving that skill ecosystems are a viable surface for denial-of-wallet attacks.
items.bottom_line: Skill ecosystems in coding agents introduce a practical and effective surface for resource-exhaustion attacks that are distinct from traditional security vulnerabilities.

claims.text: SkillBloat achieved an average best token amplification of up to 10.1455x.
claims.support_span: SkillBloat achieves 5.4184x-10.1455x average best amplification across multiple coding-agent target configurations.

claims.text: The attack uses a two-phase framework involving initial screening and LLM-guided refinement.
claims.support_span: We present SkillBloat, a two-phase framework that first screens a library of diverse attack-type conditions across multiple amplification mechanisms and then refines the strongest candidate through LLM-guided full-document skill rewriting.

claims.text: Iterative optimization provides additional benefit beyond initial attack-type selection.
claims.support_span: An ablation shows that the second-stage refinement loop consistently improves average best amplification over Phase 1 attack-type screening alone

items.title: How Reliable Are NVD CWE Labels? A Large-Scale Semantic Audit with Seclometry
items.one_liner: A large-scale semantic audit of NVD CWE labels reveals that only half match code-grounded semantics, exposing structural metadata noise.
items.summary: CWE labels in the National Vulnerability Database serve as foundational ground truth for vulnerability search, scanning tools, and prioritization, yet their reliability has rarely been measured at scale. Researchers built CWEAgent, an auditing instrument based on 'seclometry' to evaluate CWE labeling quality across code semantics. When applied to 15,556 open-source CVEs from 2017 to 2026, the tool found that only 49.70% of NVD CWE labels precisely matched code-grounded labels, while 3.63% were evidence-inconsistent errors. The study highlights that CWE noise is a structural metadata issue rather than isolated annotation mistakes, with evidence-inconsistent labels increasing over time.
items.bottom_line: Security tools and scanners relying strictly on NVD CWE labels must account for widespread structural inaccuracy and metadata noise.

items.title: Towards Automated Cyber Threat Intelligence Elicitation in Underground Forums
items.one_liner: DarkBot is a multi-agent LLM system that actively elicits cyber threat intelligence from underground forums without detection or suspension.
items.summary: Gathering cyber threat intelligence from underground forums has become harder due to migration toward private spaces, rendering passive monitoring methods less effective. To counter this, researchers developed DarkBot, a multi-agent LLM-based system designed for active CTI elicitation in underground forums. The system organizes eleven specialized agents into blocks handling engagement gating, MITRE ATT&CK-driven context-aware question generation, and linguistic style adaptation. In evaluations across CrimeBB conversations and live forum deployments, the system successfully elicited CTI-relevant disclosures without triggering moderator interventions or account suspensions.
items.bottom_line: Active multi-agent systems can successfully extract cyber threat intelligence from hard-to-reach underground forums where passive monitoring fails.

claims.text: DarkBot decomposes the interaction task across eleven specialized agents organized into three functional blocks: engagement gating for relevance and safety filtering, context-aware question generation driven by MITRE ATT&CK tactics, and linguistic style adaptation to better align with real forum users.

items.title: Scalable PII Discovery in Mobile App Databases via Hypothesis-Driven Search
items.one_liner: A highly efficient tool for automating PII discovery in mobile forensics, directly relevant to DFIR and privacy auditing.
items.summary: This research presents a hypothesis-driven agentic framework for discovering personally identifiable information (PII) in complex mobile forensic databases. The system uses an agent to rank candidate table-column regions and probe sampled values, maintaining a memory of evidence to refine its search. This approach significantly reduces the need for exhaustive inspection of heterogeneous SQLite schemas. Testing on Android and iOS databases from the Cellebrite CTF corpus showed that Gemini 2.5 Pro could achieve a 94.5% F1 score while reducing the search space by nearly 80%.
items.bottom_line: Agentic, hypothesis-driven search can reduce the manual extraction search space in mobile forensic databases by 80% while maintaining high accuracy.

items.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
items.one_liner: SecOPD provides token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, dropping prompt injection attack success rates significantly on LLM agents.
items.summary: Prompt injection remains a major threat to AI agents interacting with external data sources like emails or files, and existing defensive fine-tuning methods often fail because they rely on coarse sequence-level feedback. To provide more granular supervision, researchers proposed Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD), which supplies token-level feedback by scoring rollouts with an initialization model on clean inputs. Using this method, a defended Qwen3.6-27B model achieved a low 9.0% attack success rate against PISmith adaptive prompt injections compared to 94.0% for prior state-of-the-art Meta-SecAlign. Furthermore, the defense generalized effectively to unseen agentic tool-calling scenarios.
items.bottom_line: Token-level feedback via Secure On-Policy Distillation dramatically reduces prompt injection success rates compared to sequence-level tuning.

claims.text: Our defended Qwen3.6-27B achieves a 9.0% ASR against the SoTA PISmith adaptive prompt injections, compared to 94.0% for the prior SoTA, Meta-SecAlign.

items.title: Closed-loop AI achieves certifiable engineering design
items.one_liner: The AI Engineer couples LLMs with deterministic physics solvers to achieve certified, optimized physical engineering designs.
items.summary: While agentic AI has advanced scientific discovery and coding, complex physical engineering design remains challenging because candidates must simultaneously satisfy multiple mechanical constraints. Researchers introduced The AI Engineer, an agentic framework coupling LLMs to deterministic engineering backends and solvers like CalculiX in a closed loop. An automated reviewer scores each design across five dimensions calibrated on 11 floating-wind projects, terminating search only when composite scores reach high thresholds. The certified engineering design successfully passed an external Approval in Principle from the China Classification Society, outperforming human baselines by reducing steel mass and unit capital cost by 8.1% each.
items.bottom_line: Closed-loop AI integration with deterministic physics solvers can successfully generate certifiable, cost-optimized physical engineering structures.

items.title: Connecting the Dots: Securing the Overlooked Corners of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Supply Chain
items.one_liner: The ChainDrop worm's ability to backdoor VS Code and Claude Code directly impacts developers using AI-assisted tooling and modern CI/CD pipelines.
items.summary: The ChainDrop npm worm has infected over 400 packages, targeting developer environments and CI/CD pipelines to steal credentials and self-propagate. The malware uses a three-step chain to scrape OIDC tokens from GitHub Actions runners and modify local developer tool configurations, such as VS Code's tasks.json and Claude Code. By establishing persistence in these tools, attackers maintain access even after a build completes. The worm manages its command-and-control infrastructure via Ethereum blockchain transactions, making it highly resilient to traditional takedowns.
key_facts: Targeted Tools: VS Code, Claude Code, GitHub Actions
Theft Targets: OIDC tokens, cloud secrets, developer credentials
items.bottom_line: Attackers are now backdooring developer tools like VS Code and Claude Code to maintain persistent access to the software supply chain.

claims.support_span: ChainDrop secured long-term persistence by establishing cross-linked hooks directly inside developer tools like VS Code and Claude Code, while managing its entire command-and-control (C2) infrastructure dynamically through Ethereum blockchain transactions.

items.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Blackwell Set a New Standard for Agentic AI Performance per Watt
items.one_liner: Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Blackwell architectures set new efficiency standards for high-token agentic AI workloads.
items.summary: Nvidia previewed its Vera Rubin NVL72 architecture, demonstrating up to 30x higher AI-factory throughput per megawatt compared to the GB300 NVL72 when running complex, multi-step agentic workflows. As AI usage shifts from single-turn prompts to stateful, multi-step agentic execution—which OpenRouter's report shows consumes 15 times the tokens of standard chat—hardware benchmarks must account for long-context prefill, KV-cache reuse, and tool-call interruptions. SemiAnalysis's open-source AgentX benchmark evaluates these dynamic workloads by replaying recorded Claude Code sessions. The results highlight how Blackwell and Rubin architectures dramatically improve energy efficiency and throughput for agentic-coding inference.

items.one_liner: An API password-reset endpoint allowed unauthenticated mass account takeover simply by modifying the user ID parameter in the request body.
items.summary: During an authorized API penetration test, a researcher discovered a critical mass account takeover vulnerability within a password-reset endpoint. The backend API trusted client-supplied JSON parameters—specifically the User_Id field—without verifying authorization, session tokens, current passwords, or OTPs. By substituting the User_Id value, an attacker could silently change the password of any registered user on the platform. The flaw highlights the severe risks of client-side trust in sensitive authentication workflows.
items.bottom_line: Failing to validate server-side session authorization against user identifiers in password reset APIs allows full account compromise.

items.title: VU#308749: Remote Code Execution and Arbitrary File Read Vulnerabilities in Kaltura Servers
items.one_liner: This is a zero-day RCE in a widely used video platform library that requires immediate network-level mitigation.
items.summary: The Kaltura HTML5 Player Library contains two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-19912 and CVE-2026-19913, that enable remote code execution (RCE) and arbitrary file reads. The flaws stem from insecure PHP deserialization in the mwEmbedLoader.php endpoint, which accepts user-controlled URLs and parameters without validation. Attackers can use these to read sensitive files like database credentials or execute commands as the web-server user. Because the vendor has not yet provided a patch, users are advised to restrict or disable access to the vulnerable endpoint immediately.
key_facts: Affected Versions: html5lib v2.45, v2.103 and earlier
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated RCE and file read vulnerabilities are present in Kaltura servers with no official patch available, requiring manual mitigation by disabling the affected endpoint.

items.title: Caste divide makes summer more scorching in dry Indian region
items.one_liner: Severe heatwaves and water scarcity in Bundelkhand are intensifying caste discrimination and access barriers for Dalit families.
items.summary: In the drought-prone Bundelkhand region spanning Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, extreme summer temperatures exceeding 40°C have exacerbated severe water scarcity caused by dry government water schemes and dropping groundwater tables. Residents rely heavily on communal handpumps, leading to intense competition during early morning hours. For Dalits belonging to marginalized communities like the Valmikis, this scarcity intensifies entrenched caste discrimination, as they must wait until upper-caste residents finish using the pumps and frequently face ritualistic cleansing of the water sources afterward. While local officials and dominant-caste residents deny caste-based discrimination, Dalit families report ongoing social exclusion and fear of targeting amid the resource crunch.
key_facts: Region: Bundelkhand (Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh)
items.bottom_line: Climate-driven water scarcity in rural India is amplifying historical caste divides and friction at public water points.

items.summary: India and China held their 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question in Beijing, with National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi meeting for extensive discussions. Both sides focused on advancing negotiations for border delimitation along parts of the Line of Actual Control, improving border management mechanisms, and expanding transboundary cooperation. The talks reviewed progress made since last year's agreement to establish an early harvest working group for border delimitation. Both officials underscored that maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas has allowed bilateral relations to steadily return to normalcy. The discussions also served as preparation ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's anticipated visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit in September.

Key participants: Ajit Doval and Wang Yi

items.title: China’s Xi Jinping may attend BRICS summit in Delhi next month with large delegation
items.one_liner: Xi Jinping's expected visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit signals a crucial step in normalising India-China ties post-2020.
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is likely to visit New Delhi on September 12 and 13 to attend the BRICS summit, marking his first visit to India since 2019. The potential visit follows significant bilateral efforts to stabilise relations and resume direct flights, visas, and pilgrimages after the border standoff that began in 2020. An advance Chinese security team has arrived in New Delhi, and Xi is expected to travel with a large delegation of officials and business representatives. While over 50,000 troops remain deployed along the Line of Actual Control and complete de-escalation has not occurred, both nations have worked toward rapprochement. items.title: A Tale of Two SOCs: Insights From Two Red Team Assessments
items.one_liner: This provides concrete examples of how specific defensive postures, such as rapid detection and isolation, play out during real-world simulated attacks.
items.summary: CISA released an advisory comparing two red team assessments to highlight differences in defensive maturity. In Organization A, the red team achieved full domain compromise and accessed sensitive business systems and cloud resources without detection. In Organization B, defenders quickly detected the initial compromise and later isolated a bastion host when the team attempted to move into the OT DMZ. The report emphasizes that proactive detection and isolation capabilities were the primary factors in containing the simulated breach at Organization B.
key_facts: Sectors: Government Services (Org A), Water and Wastewater (Org B)
items.bottom_line: Rapid detection of initial access and lateral movement is the primary differentiator between a contained incident and a total network compromise.

items.title: ReliaQuest confirms failed data-theft attack after ShinyHunters breach
items.one_liner: This incident demonstrates that even with stolen credentials and MFA approval, device-trust controls can prevent a full breach.
items.summary: Cybersecurity firm ReliaQuest confirmed a social engineering attack by the ShinyHunters group that successfully phished an employee's SSO credentials. The attackers used a lookalike domain (reliaquest.claims) and vishing to trick the employee into approving an MFA push notification, granting temporary view-only access to the identity dashboard. However, ReliaQuest's device-trust controls successfully blocked subsequent attempts to access internal applications or customer data. The company has since terminated the sessions, reset credentials, and audited its security controls to ensure no persistence was established.
items.bottom_line: Strong device-trust and conditional access policies successfully mitigated a credential theft and MFA bypass attempt by a sophisticated threat group.

items.title: Critical Keycloak Password Reset Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Take Over Any Account
items.one_liner: This critical identity provider flaw allows trivial account takeover of any user, including admins, without any user interaction.
items.summary: Red Hat and the Keycloak project have patched a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-18963, which allows unauthenticated remote attackers to take over any user account, including administrative ones. The flaw resides in the reset-credentials authentication flow, where improper state validation allows an attacker to bypass the required email action token. Users of upstream Keycloak should update to version 26.7.2, while Red Hat build customers have specific updates for versions 26.4 and 26.6. If immediate patching is not possible, the recommended mitigation is to disable the Forgot password functionality across all realms.
items.bottom_line: Any unauthenticated attacker can reset any Keycloak account password without email access, making immediate updates or disabling the password reset feature mandatory.

items.title: 14 Trojanized npm Packages Drop RedC2 4.0 Linux Backdoor With AI-Assisted C2
items.one_liner: This highlights the critical risk of supply-chain attacks in the npm ecosystem where functional packages mask sophisticated cross-platform implants.
items.summary: Fourteen trojanized npm packages disguised as calendar and streak utilities were discovered delivering the RedC2 4.0 Linux backdoor. The malware executes immediately upon module import, even as a transitive dependency, without requiring install hooks. Once active, the 'RedShell' beacon facilitates surveillance, credential theft, and remote command execution via /bin/sh. The framework has been active since 2025 and is marketed as a cross-platform toolkit for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
items.bottom_line: Importing even a single transitive dependency from this set can compromise a Linux host with a persistent, feature-rich backdoor.

items.title: Weedhack Malware Spreads via Fake Minecraft Clients and SEO Poisoning
items.one_liner: This highlights the use of AI to scale phishing infrastructure and the continued effectiveness of SEO poisoning for malware delivery.
items.summary: A malware family known as Weedhack is being distributed to gamers via fake Minecraft client websites that use SEO poisoning to outrank legitimate sources. Attackers are leveraging AI-powered website builders like Lovable to quickly create convincing clones of popular projects, including Glazed Client and Radium Client. items.title: Scott Bessent’s bond buyback strategy draws criticism from Druckenmiller, JPMorgan: ‘Paying mortgage with credit card’
items.one_liner: Criticism of US Treasury bond buybacks highlights growing market friction over debt sustainability and price intervention.
items.summary: The US Treasury's decision to double its long-term bond purchases to $4 billion following a 30-year yield spike has drawn sharp criticism from prominent investors like Stanley Druckenmiller and JPMorgan's James Sullivan. Druckenmiller condemned the buyback strategy as political price management that compromises the credibility of the Treasury market. Meanwhile, JPMorgan's Sullivan likened the intervention to 'paying a mortgage with a credit card,' noting it fails to address the underlying issue of surging debt supply. Both critics emphasize that governments cannot permanently defend asset prices against fundamental market supply and demand imbalances without addressing primary fiscal deficits.
